correctness.rationale: Li's theta reduction f(n)≡[q^n]Θ(q)^2 (mod 3) holds formally. For N=20n+9, pair (a,b) maps bijectively to X=5(a+b)−3,Y=5(a−b) with X²+Y²=N, X≡2 mod5,Y≡0 mod5 and theta sign (−1)^Y. Every Gaussian-unit orbit for odd N≡4 mod5 has exactly one canonical representative. In Z[i], inert p≡3 mod4 of odd exponent forbid orbits; altering a split prime factor for p≡1,9 mod20 preserves Y parity, while p≡13,17 mod20 flips it after canonical quarter-turn. Thus a local alternating exponent sum annihilates odd exponents of the latter; surviving |g(n)|=∏_{p≡1,9 mod20}(e_p+1). Mod3 adds e_p≠2 mod3. Independent direct partition dynamic programming, Gaussian norm sums and factorization agree for n=0..400 including n=31,N=629; unlimited theorem follows Gaussian UFD and parity.
